finding.claim: OS command injection: the unauthenticated GET /ping handler concatenates req.query.host into a shell command string passed to child_process.exec, so shell metacharacters run arbitrary commands.
finding.source: req.query.host (HTTP query parameter on GET /ping, unauthenticated)
finding.sink: exec("ping -c 1 " + req.query.host) at tools.js:7, which runs via /bin/sh -c

trace.note: Route handler for GET /ping registered with no auth middleware
req.query.host is concatenated unsanitized into the shell command and passed to exec()
Command stdout is returned in the response, so output is visible to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No validation, allowlist, or escaping of host. No auth middleware anywhere in the app (app.use is never called). exec uses a shell, not argv. The err check at line 8 only handles the error response and does not constrain input. An array-valued query param (?host[]=x) would be coerced to string, which does not help as a guard.

verdict.reason: tools.js:7 passes "ping -c 1 " + req.query.host to exec() (shell) with no validation, and the route at tools.js:6 has no auth, so an anonymous caller can inject commands. Output returns at tools.js:11 only on success, but injected commands still run regardless.
